title: Monitoring Protein Adsorption with Solid-state Nanopores
protocol: Bring the FEI Tecnai F20 S/TEM to an acceleration voltage of 200 kV.
Load a 20 nm thick SPI silicon nitride window grid into the TEM sample holder.
Clean the holder with Oxygen plasma for 30 seconds.
Load the cleaned sample into the S/TEM and allow for vacuum pumping down.
Find the nitride window in bright-field TEM mode on the Ronchigram.
Properly align and focus the sample.
Switch the S/TEM into STEM mode.
Image the sample using the HAADF (or equivalent) detector to ensure proper alignment.
Set the Monochromator to a low value, if available.
Select an appropriate spot size for drilling the nanopore.
Adjust the STEM alignments as necessary.
Focus the nitride membrane at a magnification of x1.3M.
Monitor the Ronchigram for fine focusing.
Wait for sample stabilization if movement occurs; blank the electron beam during waiting periods.
Place the electron probe on the sample and begin drilling.
Periodically check the nanopore formation using HAADF detector scanning.
Adjust the position of the electron probe to maintain focus over the nanopore if it drifts.
Identify nanopore formation by observing changes in Ronchigram appearance.
Observe a shimmering disappearance indicating pore formation; move Ronchigram slightly out of focus for Fresnel fringe visibility.
Take an image of the nanopore using HAADF detector.
Perform an intensity profile analysis on the nanopore image to estimate diameter.
Enlarge the nanopore by moving the electron probe along its edges.
Set the nanopore to a desired diameter and switch S/TEM to TEM mode.
Adjust Monochromator to standard setting for imaging.
Confirm nanopore size using bright-field TEM imaging.
De-gas de-ionized water containing 1 M KCl, 10 mM potassium phosphate, pH 7.4.
Place solutions under vacuum and sonicate for 20 minutes.
Place the nanopore-containing silicon nitride chip into a 10 ml Pyrex beaker.
Set up hotplate in fume hood at 100°C.
Clean the nanopore chip with piranha solution using a glass pipette.
Add 3 ml sulfuric acid to container.
Carefully add 1 ml hydrogen peroxide to make piranha solution.
Allow nanopore chip to soak for 10 minutes.
Remove piranha solution from beaker and store properly.
Fill the beaker with de-gassed, de-ionized water using a clean glass pipette.
Empty beaker of water and repeat at least 5 times.
Remove the nanopore chip with clean tweezers and dry by light suction immediately.
Seal the nanopore chip into the chamber.
Connect Ag/AgCl electrodes to the chamber.
Apply transmembrane potential across electrodes.
Monitor current response using Axon 200B patch-clamp amplifier in voltage-clamp mode.
Construct an I/V curve from the measurements.
Ensure the I/V curve is highly linear when using 1 M KCl.
Check if the nanopore displays a linear I/V curve and stable open current.
Repeat piranha washing if the conductance is too low or the open current is not stable.
Perform control experiments with a single-nanopore membrane or parallel array of nanopores to monitor current in buffer conditions lacking protein sample.
Use high purity-level buffer (purity > 99.9%) for control experiments.
Choose a buffer that does not produce single-channel events when interacting with the solid-state nanopore.
Obtain a high-purity protein sample using standard protein chemistry procedures.
Check the purity of the protein sample by SDS-PAGE gel analysis and high-resolution mass spectrometry.
Add purified protein sample to the grounded bath of the chamber.
Allow time for the sample to diffuse throughout the bath.
Apply a positive voltage bias of 200 mV across the nitride nanopore.
Increase the concentration of the protein if no signal is observed.
Use higher voltages to improve the signal-to-noise ratio.
Monitor transient current deflections as indicators of protein events.
Observe long-lived changes in baseline current for protein adsorption.
Wash the silicon nitride nanopore with piranha solution.
Secure the washed nanopore in the chamber.
Add amine directly to the chamber bath containing 0.5 M TBACl as supporting electrolyte and anhydrous MeOH as solvent.
Apply a 400 mV voltage bias across the chamber.
Monitor monolayer formation by measuring the current drop.
